_README.description: PharmaPy compound database for Bachmann-process RDX/HMX synthesis train. Each species must have at minimum: mw, rho_liq, rho_solid.
_README.cp_liq_form: Cp(T) = A + B*T + C*T^2 + D*T^3 + E*T^4  [J/mol/K], T in [K]
_README.cp_solid_form: Cp(T) = A + B*T + C*T^2 + D*T^3 + E*T^4  [J/mol/K], T in [K]
_README.visc_liq_form: mu(T) = A * exp(B/T + C*T + D*T^2)        [Pa.s],    T in [K]
_README.p_vap_form: ln(P) = A - B/(T - C)                      [Pa],      T in [K]
_README.solubility_form: S(T) = A + B*T + C*T^2 + D*T^3            [kg/m^3],  T in [K]

confidence_key.HIGH: Directly measured value from NIST, Perry's, or peer-reviewed literature
confidence_key.MEDIUM: Derived by fitting to 2-3 data points or converted from another equation form
confidence_key.LOW: Group-contribution estimate or rough engineering approximation; verify before use

Nitric_Acid._notes: Pure (anhydrous) HNO3. CAS 7697-37-2. Decomposes before reaching its true critical point; t_crit/p_crit are group-contribution estimates. For 68% commercial grade use rho_liq ~1400 kg/m^3.
Nitric_Acid._t_crit_conf: LOW - Joback estimate; HNO3 decomposes ~200 C so true Tc is inaccessible
Nitric_Acid._p_crit_conf: LOW - Joback estimate [Pa]; literature range 6.2-7.2 MPa
Nitric_Acid._cp_liq_conf: MEDIUM - Perry's Handbook ~109.9 J/mol/K at 298 K; temperature dependence sparse
Nitric_Acid._cp_solid_conf: LOW - Approximate for solid HNO3 near mp (231 K); ~60-70 J/mol/K
Nitric_Acid._rho_liq_conf: HIGH - Pure anhydrous HNO3: 1512-1513 kg/m^3 at 20 C (Wikipedia/multiple SDS)
Nitric_Acid._rho_solid_conf: LOW - White crystals (mp = -42 C); limited literature data ~1.9 g/cm^3
Nitric_Acid._visc_liq_conf: MEDIUM - Andrade fit: mu(298K)=7.61e-4 Pa.s (Wikipedia/Fisher MSDS), mu(273K)~1.0e-3 Pa.s
Nitric_Acid._p_vap_conf: MEDIUM - Antoine fit ln[Pa]=A-B/(T-C); anchored to bp=356.15 K. Replace with DIPPR if available.
Nitric_Acid._delta_hvap_conf: HIGH - NIST WebBook: 38.6 kJ/mol at 312 K (Holeci 1966)
Nitric_Acid._surf_tension_conf: MEDIUM - ~41 mN/m at 20 C; confirm against CRC/DIPPR for your concentration
Nitric_Acid.source: NIST WebBook CAS 7697-37-2; Wikipedia; Fisher MSDS; Perry's Handbook

Water._notes: Pure liquid water H2O. CAS 7732-18-5. All values are well-established from IAPWS-IF97.
Water._cp_liq_conf: HIGH - NIST: 75.3 J/mol/K at 298 K; constant approximation valid +/-30 K
Water._cp_solid_conf: HIGH - Ice Ih at 0 C: 38.1 J/mol/K (CRC Handbook)
Water._rho_solid_conf: HIGH - Ice Ih at 0 C: 917 kg/m^3 (CRC Handbook)
Water._visc_liq_conf: MEDIUM - Andrade fit: mu(298K)=8.9e-4, mu(313K)=6.5e-4 Pa.s (NIST)
Water._p_vap_conf: HIGH - Standard Antoine: ln(P[Pa])=23.197-3816.44/(T[K]-46.13). Gives 101325 Pa at 373.15 K. Valid 274-373 K.
Water._delta_hvap_conf: HIGH - NIST WebBook: ~44.0 kJ/mol at 298 K
Water._surf_tension_conf: HIGH - CRC Handbook: 72.0 mN/m at 25 C
Water.source: NIST WebBook CAS 7732-18-5; IAPWS-IF97; CRC Handbook

Hexamine._notes: Hexamethylenetetramine (HMTA), C6H12N4, CAS 100-97-0. Sublimes at ~280 C under atmospheric pressure and does NOT have a conventional liquid phase. rho_liq and cp_liq are effective/estimated values for use when hexamine is modelled as a dissolved component in solvent. Replace with measured solution properties where possible.
Hexamine._t_crit_conf: LOW - Joback estimate; sublimes/decomposes before critical point
Hexamine._cp_liq_conf: LOW - Effective value for solution; no true liquid. Estimated from cp_solid +30%
Hexamine._cp_solid_conf: MEDIUM - Literature consensus: ~170 J/mol/K at 298 K (Cheméo/NIST TRC)
Hexamine._rho_liq_conf: LOW - No true liquid phase; estimated effective solution density ~1.1 g/cm^3. Replace with measured value for your concentration.
Hexamine._visc_liq_conf: LOW - Rough estimate for hexamine in solution. Replace with measured viscosity.
Hexamine._p_vap_conf: LOW - SDS: vapor pressure <0.01 mmHg (<1.3 Pa) at 20 C. Approximate Antoine; replace with sublimation data.
Hexamine._delta_hvap_conf: LOW - Approximate sublimation enthalpy ~80 kJ/mol; no confirmed literature value
Hexamine._surf_tension_conf: LOW - Estimated for solution; no data for pure liquid
Hexamine.source: ChemicalBook CAS 100-97-0; Cheméo; NIST TRC; multiple supplier SDS

RDX._notes: Cyclotrimethylenetrinitramine (hexogen), C3H6N6O6, CAS 121-82-4. mp ~204 C; decomposes above ~210 C. Liquid phase is thermally unstable. rho_solid is crystal density (alpha/beta-form). rho_liq is estimated for the melt just above mp. All liquid properties are LOW confidence.
RDX._t_crit_conf: LOW - Joback estimate; RDX decomposes well before this
RDX._cp_liq_conf: LOW - Estimated for liquid RDX near mp; cp_solid ~175 scaled +30%
RDX._cp_solid_conf: MEDIUM - LASL Explosive Property Data: ~175 J/mol/K at 298 K; range 170-180 J/mol/K in literature
RDX._rho_liq_conf: LOW - Estimated liquid density near mp (~204 C); ~1.54 g/cm^3 from volume expansion estimate
RDX._rho_solid_conf: HIGH - Global Ordnance spec/multiple sources: 1.814 g/cm^3 at 20 C (crystal, alpha-form)
RDX._visc_liq_conf: LOW - Very rough estimate near mp; no reliable data
RDX._p_vap_conf: LOW - Extremely low sublimation pressure (~4e-5 Pa at 25 C estimated); Antoine is approximate only
RDX._delta_hvap_conf: MEDIUM - Sublimation enthalpy ~101 kJ/mol from Zeman (2006) Thermochim. Acta and Zuckerman et al.
RDX._surf_tension_conf: LOW - Estimated from liquid organic nitroamine analogs
RDX.source: NIST WebBook CAS 121-82-4; Global Ordnance datasheet; LASL Explosive Property Data; Zeman (2006) Thermochim. Acta

HMX._notes: Cyclotetramethylenetetranitramine (octogen), C4H8N8O8, CAS 2691-41-0. mp ~281 C (beta-form); decomposes ~300 C. Four polymorphs exist (alpha/beta/gamma/delta); beta is the stable high-density form used in explosives. rho_solid is for beta-HMX.
HMX._t_crit_conf: LOW - Joback estimate; HMX decomposes before reaching critical point
HMX._cp_liq_conf: LOW - Estimated for liquid near mp; cp_solid ~220 scaled +27%
HMX._cp_solid_conf: MEDIUM - LASL Explosive Property Data / literature: ~220 J/mol/K at 298 K for beta-HMX
HMX._rho_liq_conf: LOW - Estimated: crystal density 1.903 g/cm^3 with ~10% expansion at melt ~1.72 g/cm^3
HMX._rho_solid_conf: HIGH - ChemicalBook/multiple literature: beta-HMX crystal 1.903 g/cm^3 (most cited value)
HMX._visc_liq_conf: LOW - Very rough estimate near mp; no reliable data
HMX._p_vap_conf: LOW - Extremely low sublimation pressure (<1e-7 Pa at 25 C estimated); Antoine approximate only
HMX._delta_hvap_conf: MEDIUM - Sublimation enthalpy ~127 kJ/mol; Zeman (2006) Thermochim. Acta; Rosen & Dickinson literature
HMX._surf_tension_conf: LOW - Estimated from liquid nitramine analogs
HMX.source: ChemicalBook CAS 2691-41-0; Wikipedia HMX; LASL Explosive Property Data; Zeman (2006) Thermochim. Acta; Austin Powder SDS

HDN._notes: Hexamethylenetetramine dinitrate (hexamine dinitrate), C6H12N4.2HNO3, CAS 18423-69-3. Bachmann-process intermediate formed when hexamine contacts HNO3 below 15 C. CRITICAL SAFETY: DSC shows melting at 170.5 C followed by exothermic decomposition at 174 C and 200.5 C (Turhan 2013) -- only 3.5 C window between melt and runaway. The liquid phase must NOT be maintained; process temperatures above 150 C must be avoided. All liquid properties are LOW confidence and provided only to allow model initialization.
HDN._t_crit_conf: LOW - Joback estimate; HDN decomposes well below this temperature
HDN._cp_liq_conf: LOW - Estimated for molten HDN (~170 C); no literature data; scaled from cp_solid
HDN._cp_solid_conf: LOW - Estimated from molecular weight and group-contribution analogy (hexamine + ammonium nitrate fractions)
HDN._rho_liq_conf: LOW - Estimated near mp (170.5 C); no literature data; analogous to similar organic nitrate salts
HDN._rho_solid_conf: LOW - Estimated from analogous organic nitrate salts (~1.6-1.7 g/cm^3); no direct measurement found in open literature
HDN._visc_liq_conf: LOW - Rough estimate for molten HDN; no data available
HDN._p_vap_conf: LOW - Extremely low vapor pressure (hygroscopic solid); approximate placeholder only
HDN._delta_hvap_conf: LOW - Approximate; true hvap is not meaningful since material decomposes near mp. Estimated from Gilpin & Winkler (1952) thermochemistry data.
HDN._tref_hvap_conf: HIGH - mp from DSC: 170.5 C = 443.65 K (Turhan et al. 2013)
HDN.source: Turhan et al. (2013) Propellants Explosives Pyrotechnics DOI:10.1002/prep.201200162; Gilpin & Winkler Can. J. Chem. 1952 30 743

Acetic_Anhydride._notes: Acetic anhydride, (CH3CO)2O, C4H6O3, CAS 108-24-7. One of the two Bachmann-process solvents/reagents. Reacts exothermically with water to form acetic acid; monitor water content carefully in process.
Acetic_Anhydride._t_crit_conf: HIGH - Perry's Chemical Engineers Handbook: 606 K
Acetic_Anhydride._p_crit_conf: HIGH - Perry's Chemical Engineers Handbook: 4.67 MPa
Acetic_Anhydride._cp_liq_conf: MEDIUM - Perry's Table 2-151: ~181 J/mol/K at 298 K for liquid
Acetic_Anhydride._cp_solid_conf: LOW - Estimated; mp=-73 C; no direct literature value found
Acetic_Anhydride._rho_liq_conf: HIGH - Multiple SDS/literature: 1.082 g/cm^3 at 20 C
Acetic_Anhydride._rho_solid_conf: LOW - Estimated from liquid density with ~10% increase at solidification; mp=-73 C
Acetic_Anhydride._visc_liq_conf: MEDIUM - Andrade fit: mu(20C)=0.903 cP, mu(40C)=0.601 cP (Cheméo/Sigma-Aldrich)
Acetic_Anhydride._p_vap_conf: MEDIUM - Converted from Perry's Antoine (log10[mmHg]=7.14948-1444.718/(T[C]+199.817)) to ln[Pa]=A-B/(T[K]-C). Gives 101.3 kPa at bp=412.7 K (139.6 C).
Acetic_Anhydride._delta_hvap_conf: MEDIUM - Perry's Handbook: ~42.5 kJ/mol at normal bp (412.7 K)
Acetic_Anhydride._tref_hvap_conf: HIGH - Normal boiling point 139.55 C = 412.7 K
Acetic_Anhydride._surf_tension_conf: HIGH - CRC Handbook: 32.9 mN/m at 20 C
Acetic_Anhydride.source: Perry's Chemical Engineers Handbook 8th Ed.; NIST WebBook CAS 108-24-7; Cheméo; CRC Handbook

Acetic_Acid._notes: Glacial acetic acid, CH3COOH, C2H4O2, CAS 64-19-7. Co-solvent in Bachmann process; also produced as by-product. Freezing point 16.5 C -- may solidify in cold process lines. rho_solid given for monoclinic crystals near mp.
Acetic_Acid._cp_liq_conf: MEDIUM - Perry's Handbook: ~123.5 J/mol/K (~2.05 J/g/K) near 298 K
Acetic_Acid._cp_solid_conf: MEDIUM - CRC Handbook: solid acetic acid ~88 J/mol/K near mp (289.65 K)
Acetic_Acid._rho_liq_conf: HIGH - NIST/SDS: 1.049 g/cm^3 at 20 C for glacial acetic acid
Acetic_Acid._rho_solid_conf: MEDIUM - CRC Handbook: monoclinic solid ~1.266 g/cm^3 near mp (16.5 C)
Acetic_Acid._visc_liq_conf: MEDIUM - Andrade fit: mu(25C)=1.056 cP (Sigma-Aldrich), mu(60C)~0.60 cP (literature)
Acetic_Acid._p_vap_conf: MEDIUM - Converted from Perry's Antoine (log10[mmHg]=7.38782-1533.313/(T[C]+222.309)) to ln[Pa]=A-B/(T[K]-C). Gives 101.3 kPa at bp=391.1 K (117.9 C).
Acetic_Acid._delta_hvap_conf: HIGH - NIST WebBook: ~51.6 kJ/mol at 298 K (condensed-phase enthalpy of vaporization)
Acetic_Acid._surf_tension_conf: HIGH - CRC Handbook: 27.2 mN/m at 20 C
Acetic_Acid.source: NIST WebBook CAS 64-19-7; Perry's Handbook; CRC Handbook; Sigma-Aldrich SDS

Ammonium_Nitrate._notes: Ammonium nitrate, NH4NO3, CAS 6484-52-2. Bachmann-process nitrogen source. mp ~169.6 C. PROCESS SAFETY CRITICAL: decomposes exothermically above ~210 C and can deflagrate/detonate under confinement and contamination. Five solid polymorphs exist; rho_solid is for form IV (~20 C). rho_liq is for the melt near 170 C. t_crit/p_crit are Joback estimates only.
Ammonium_Nitrate._t_crit_conf: LOW - Joback group-contribution (Cheméo): 677.44 K; AN decomposes long before this
Ammonium_Nitrate._cp_liq_conf: MEDIUM - Literature: molten AN Cp ~166 J/mol/K near 175 C (Stern & Kay J. Chem. Eng. Data)
Ammonium_Nitrate._cp_solid_conf: MEDIUM - Perry's/literature: solid AN form IV ~134 J/mol/K at 298 K
Ammonium_Nitrate._rho_liq_conf: MEDIUM - Perry's/Stern & Kay: molten AN ~1.44 g/cm^3 near mp (~175 C)
Ammonium_Nitrate._rho_solid_conf: HIGH - Perry's/CRC: solid AN form IV ~1.725 g/cm^3 at 20 C
Ammonium_Nitrate._visc_liq_conf: LOW - Andrade estimate fitted to ~2.3 mPa.s at 175 C (literature); very rough; replace with measured value
Ammonium_Nitrate._p_vap_conf: LOW - Negligible vapor pressure in normal process range; these coefficients are placeholder only (~1 Pa at 400 K)
Ammonium_Nitrate._delta_hvap_conf: LOW - Joback estimate (Cheméo): 45.24 kJ/mol; AN decomposes near/above mp so true hvap is not meaningful
Ammonium_Nitrate._surf_tension_conf: LOW - Estimated for molten AN near mp, analogous to other molten inorganic nitrates (~60-70 mN/m)
Ammonium_Nitrate.source: Perry's Chemical Engineers Handbook; Cheméo CAS 6484-52-2; Stern & Kay J. Chem. Eng. Data; CRC Handbook
